clue.text: Hollywood types who have meteoric careers?

definitions.text: Hollywood types who have meteoric careers?

parts.words: Hollywood types who have meteoric careers?
parts.note: film celebrities whose fame rises fast are named after the streaks of light seen crossing the night sky

explanation.surface: A remark about film celebrities whose careers rocket upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a definition with a pun: 'meteoric' describes a rapid career, and also literally the burning meteors whose popular name doubles as a term for screen celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteors are popularly called by this name, and the same phrase describes famous film actors.

clue.text: Price of abandoning one's policy

parts.note: the sum an insurer pays when a holder gives up a life policy before it matures, dressed as a politician dropping a principle

explanation.surface: A politician counts the cost of dropping a principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policy' reads as a political stance, but here it is an insurance policy; cashing one in early earns this payout.
explanation.definitionFit: In insurance, this is the cash refund paid when a holder gives up a policy early.

clue.text: Gold piece in circulation

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A gold coin passing from hand to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet's path going round and round the sun is a circulation in a closed loop.

clue.text: Dreadful tenor — alto I gave indulgence

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something badly done, so the singers' words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer laments that the tenor was awful, yet still put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges TENOR, ALTO and I; 'gave' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgence and this word both mean putting up with what one dislikes; they are synonyms for tolerance.

clue.text: A number, and another number — I accepted none of them

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: ether is an anaesthetic, something that makes you numb, so a 'number'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rejects two numbers offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' twice misleads: the second is pronounced with a silent b, one who numbs, giving ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of two choices, this word means not one or the other, so none of the pair.

clue.text: Specially warm area that's marked on disc

explanation.surface: A disc marked to show a warm region.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a holiday resort with reliable heat; the other is a dark patch seen on the face of our star.

clue.text: Seaweed collected by coastal gang

indicators.note: collected by means the letters are gathered up inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gang on the shore gathers seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweeds are marine plants of this simple kind, so one example names the class.

clue.text: Meagre period for leisure

parts.note: spare can mean meagre or scanty
a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: Complaining that there is little time to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Free hours away from work are synonymous with leisure.

clue.text: People with dark shades, powerful behind the scenes

explanation.surface: Sinister figures in sunglasses who pull the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally men dressed in dull grey clothes; idiomatically, faceless officials who hold hidden influence.

clue.text: Rising, move drunkenly around black cat

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: to reel is to stagger as a drunk does
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A tipsy person staggers around a black cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like getting up, but it is the noun for a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or revolt against authority.

clue.text: Elegance of good athletics contest

parts.note: a race is a running contest

explanation.surface: Praising the style shown in a fine track event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise and smooth beauty of movement are synonyms for elegance.

clue.text: Put down log

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to record in writing, as in a register or ledger.

clue.text: Expect to jump queue finally

parts.note: to hop is to jump

indicators.note: finally picks out only the closing letter of the word queue

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates pushing in at the front of a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something is to look forward to it, a synonym when anticipating.

clue.text: Israelite who may live rough

indicators.note: rough suggests something roughed up, so the letters of the word live are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tribesman of ancient Israel who might lead a hard life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who may' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was a son of Jacob and founder of a tribe of Israel.

clue.text: Relatively smooth house extension, perhaps

parts.note: taken as 'like a relative': a grandmother is a relative
flat means level and smooth

explanation.surface: Commenting that a house extension is fairly smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' reads as 'fairly', but here it points to a family member, a grandmother; 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contained annexe built for an elderly relative is a typical home extension.

clue.text: Goddess put off admitting me

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged from entering lets the speaker in.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeter is the Greek deity of the harvest and grain.

clue.text: Be rough on chap with title

parts.note: a chap is a man
a handle is slang for a title or name

explanation.surface: A man is roughed up because of his title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone roughly physically is the meaning, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Quickly putting out to grass

explanation.surface: Retiring an animal to graze in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Turfing out means ejecting someone briskly; turfing also means laying grass sods.

clue.text: Scores at one side of wicket, and scampers away

definitions.text: Scores at one side of wicket

explanation.surface: A batsman scores on the off side, then flees.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is one half of the field, so runs scored there fit; the phrase also means flees.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs off are cricket scores on the off side; as a verb phrase it means bolts or flees.

clue.text: Thrill of brief days with child

parts.note: FRIS is short for Fridays
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Delight at short days spent with a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiver of excitement is synonymous with a thrill.

clue.text: Genuine offence taken with prophet's speech

indicators.note: speech means the pieces are heard rather than written, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: an offence is a sin, and a prophet is a seer, giving sin followed by seer

explanation.surface: A real grievance against a prophet's sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offence taken' suggests resentment, but here offence is a wrongdoing, a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and honest feelings are synonymous here.

clue.text: Ladies who make it to the top in music

definitions.text: Ladies who make it to the top in music

parts.words: Ladies who make it to the top in music
parts.note: reads like successful female musicians, but means women who sing the highest vocal part

explanation.surface: Women who reach the pinnacle of the music business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The top' is not success but the highest line of choral music; the Italian plural is used.
explanation.definitionFit: These are female singers of the highest voice range, in the Italian plural form.

clue.text: Where one may play fixtures on holiday

explanation.definitionFit: A team plays fixtures at a rival ground, not at home; on holiday you are absent from home.

clue.text: Soft verge round motorway

indicators.note: round means the first piece encircles the next

parts.note: a lip is an edge or verge
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A grassy roadside strip beside a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verge' suggests the strip beside a road, fitting the motorway, but here means an edge, a lip.
explanation.definitionFit: Floppy and lacking firmness, so synonymous with soft.

clue.text: Poet as yet awaiting translation

indicators.note: translation suggests changing words into another form, so the letters of as yet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet whose work has not been translated so far.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was a celebrated Irish poet.

clue.text: Cavities in insect shown by painter

parts.note: an ant is an insect
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword painter

explanation.surface: Holes in an insect depicted by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'shown by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomical cavities or sinuses are called by this Latin plural.

clue.text: Poke right inside engine housing

indicators.note: inside means the letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: a pod is a streamlined housing for an aircraft engine

explanation.surface: A mechanic jabs at something within an engine casing.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to jab or poke.

clue.text: Milk from one? It depends on the cow

definitions.text: Milk from one? It depends on the cow

parts.words: Milk from one? It depends on the cow
parts.note: you draw milk from this organ, and it literally hangs down from the animal, a pun on depends

explanation.surface: A farmer says how much milk you get depends on the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It depends on the cow' sounds like a shrug, but 'depends' literally means hangs down from.
explanation.definitionFit: The milk-producing gland hanging below a cow is the organ described.

clue.text: Trail "cats," adapted by composer

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters of trail and cats are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre producer reworks a musical about cats.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted "cats" hints at the musical, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian baroque composer of keyboard sonatas.

clue.text: Coming to ripping finish, finally unsuccessful

explanation.surface: A story with a sensational climax ends in failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripping' reads as splendid, but it means tearing, so the first reading is finishing in rips.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, ending in disappointment; literally, finishing while torn apart.
